name: EBURP
description: The EBURP Collection resurrects LarvaLabs' earliest foray into pixel art with GURK, a 2004 8-bit mobile RPG that influenced the creation of Cryptopunks. In 2013, LarvaLabs open-sourced 92 of GURK's 16x16 px Heroes, Enemies and NPCs. EBURP meticulously encodes these open-source characters on-chain, bridging a pioneering pixel legacy to the blockchain era.

a.value: A Zombie is the rotting carcass of the deceased that, for whatever reason, was reanimated by black magic. Its bite can infect the victim with a debilitating illness.
Grath belongs to the shadowy League of Assassins. He is deadly in combat, but where his loyalties lie are uncertain.
The Giant Bear is typically docile and reclusive. However, when angered, its rage and aggression can be unmatched.
The Black Spider looks similar to the giant spider, but it possesses a venom that slows the reactions of its target, rendering them easy prey.
This Northern species is stronger, faster and deadlier than the more common varietal. Indeed, the Blue Goblin lists its temperate cousins amongst its favorite foods.
The Sea Snake looks fairly harmless, but it is not to be trifled with as its bite carries a poisonous venom.
These orcs are believed to have been transformed via evil magic and gruelling conditioning. They develop an innate ability to temporarily increase their strength, to devastating effect.
The Bugbear is a race of large and vicious humanoids. They possess the ability to regenerate their wounds, which matches well with their highly aggressive combat style.
The unnerving Cave Peeper is a very dangerous creature, with the astonishing knack of suddenly appearing right beside an unwary adventurer.
Stoic and enormous, the Clay Golem is a mindless yet effective instrument of punishment.
This species of crab is enormous and eats anything that moves. Its claws are tremendously powerful.
The Craw Fighter is a skilled and well-armored protector of the sanctity of the seas. Landlubbers, beware!
One-eyed and wicked, the Cyclops delights in tormenting creatures smaller or weaker than itself.
The Drow are a subspecies of elf that long ago abandoned the forests for the Northern taiga. Reclusive and nocturnal, they are even more adept with a bow than their arboreal cousins.
Despite its name, the Hobgoblin is more closely related to trolls than goblins. It is formidable, but fights without dignity, delivering vicious bites with its large and toothy mouth.
One of the most frightening incarnations of the undead, the Ghoul can emit a fearsome shriek that will freeze an opponent in its tracks.
Raised in the deep Shavanoth forest, Silvana is extraordinarily tough while also very talented with a bow.
Lady Alwyn was trained in an elite and secretive female fighting force called the 'Amazons'.
Gaelabeth was trained in the non-violent Druidic arts, but left the Order to pursue a wider study of the occult.
The Elf Rangers are a reclusive but loyal group of forest defenders. Adept archers, they will appear when called up on by their Ranger brethren.
Orcs are related to goblins, and are often found in their company. They are larger than goblins, but far less intelligent.
The object of many a child's nightmare, Goblins are cruel and vicious creatures. While certainly not a threat in individual combat, they can often overwhelm with sheer numbers.
Goblin Swashbucklers are trained in the breeding pits to fight more viciously than other Goblins. While this makes them a dangerous foe, it also dramatically reduces their life expectancy.
Only the largest and most fearsome goblins are granted the title of 'Goblin Warrior'. Besides being bigger, they are also generally better-equipped for combat than their weaker brethren.
Female goblins are typically recruited and trained as archers, where they become astonishingly adept, especially considering the poor quality of their bows.
There are a conspicuously large number of Goblins claiming to be monarchs, and each has legions of followers, who can be whipped into a bloodthirsty frenzy.
Small and nimble, the Goblin Scout may not be the most imposing of the goblins, but it can sneak in and do quick damage while deftly avoiding counter-attacks.
These incredible beasts are almost the size of a full-grown man. They are notoriously hard to kill.
The Goblin Shaman often accompanies large groups of goblins and orcs. It administers noxious elixirs that boost the strength of its allies.
The glorious Spider Queen can summon her numerous children with but a whisper. She also spins reinforcing webs to protect her brood.
The Ice Golem is deceptively agile, considering its blocky construction. Whilst being crushed by its fist, one should remain mindful of the second fist, which is rarely far behind.
The Ice Magi are infamous throughout the Fiefdoms for their spell-casting prowess. Intelligent and unpredictable, they can defeat an opponent a number of different ways.
The Ice Troll is not the largest of trolls, but it is skilled in hurling rocks at its opponents, and is able to protect itself at will in a sheath of hardened ice.
Small but mean, the Imp can attack very quickly, doing considerable damage before an opponent can counter-attack.
The Giant Jellyfish not only has a size advantage, but its sting delivers a poisonous toxin to its victim.
Strong, proud and resolute, Sir Rugnar will always faithfully defend his companions valiantly.
Thought to be the result of an unfortunate cross-breeding experiment, these dog-like men are diminutive, but hunt effectively in packs.
The Kobold Mystic can attack at range with spells, and uses foul magic to boost the abilities of its allies in combat.
The Kobold Fighter is a surprisingly well-trained warrior. It can wield two weapons with amazing dexterity.
Oloman is an unscrupulous warrior-for-hire. His only two motivations are self-preservation and profit.
Some legends claim that the Merfolk were the very first discoverers of sorcery, although it is disputed. The Merman Sorcerers can heal allies and summon oceanic brethren to aid in their battles.
Training with a sword underwater results in an incredible amount of precision an speed, making the Merman Swordsman a highly respected opponent in battle, both in and out of water.
The Mind Flayer is the stuff of nightmares, a merciless killer that attacks its victims' minds with agonizing psychic damage.
The mighty Minotaur is among the greatest of warriors. Few have survived hand-to-hand combat with the murderous creatures.
A Mummy is the reanimated corpse of a wealthy noble or ruler. It can move with surprising speed, and its vicious bite weakens its victim.
B'Az Aptar has broken the Oath of the Benevolent Magi and begun tinkering with the Dark Arts. But does he control the powerful undead forces, or do they control him?
The Ogre Assassins are well-trained, resulting in a quicker and more intelligent foe than a standard Ogre. Their preferred method of attack is the ambush.
The common Ogre is the scourge of civilized people everywhere, as civilized people is the food of choice for the common Ogre.
The Priestesses rule the Oliphant herd societies. They can magically summon their brethren, and can heal whole groups of compatriots at a time.
The Oliphant Sentry's training imbues it with a maniacal instinct to preserve the well-being of the herd. It can fly off in to a wild rage when it feels that its brethren are threatened.
The Charger is not a quick-witted Oliphant, but it relies on its superior speed and size to carry the day.
Oliphants are a race of elephant-like humanoids. They are fiercely reclusive and suspicious of humans.
A Phantom is an undead spirit that is only partially present in the corporeal realm. It attacks with magic at range, yet is itself very resistant to magical effects.
Incredibly dedicated, Feraldan began learning the skill of archery as soon as he was old enough to hold a bow.
One of the most dangerous animals ever documented, the combustible venom of the Fire Snake can engulf hapless opponents in blistering flames.
The Spitting Spider can project acidic venom with astounding accuracy over great distances. It's an insect worth avoiding.
The Rock Golem attacks by hurling the very stuff that it is made of: rocks. Its geologic construction has few weaknesses.

Skeletons are crude and artless undead re-animations. They are easily dispatched in hand-to-hand combat, but have the annoying habit of standing at a distance and lobbing bones plucked from their own body at their opponents.
The Skeleton Guard is a better-equipped and more resolute skeletal automaton than the garden-variety. They are not to be trifled with.
Unlike most raised spirits, the Skeleton Wizards willingly joined the undead, and are hence more powerful. They can summon skeletons and weaken their opponents with their gaze.
While not poisonous, the Giant Snake has been known to take down and devour very large prey, including people!
While not as large as its warm-weather cousins, the Snow Ogre is no less dangerous. It will snap quite suddenly into a rage, attacking its enemies with wild abandon.
A mysterious undead form, the insidious Spectre is nearly invisible, making it a very difficult opponent to defeat.
Possessed and controlled by the Merfolk, these poor, everyday fish have been coerced to take up arms against all who walk on dry land.
Trolls are large, nasty and devious humanoids. Their preferred method of attack is to hurl large rocks at their opponent, with devastating efficiency.
The ancient Treant Elders can summon the forces of nature to spontaneously sprout roots, entrapping its adversaries.
Once regarded as gentle giants, the Treants have recently turned against humankind, blaming them for the degradation of the forests.
While Two-headed Trolls are notorious for their continuous self-bickering, this belies their coordination and skill in combat.
No details are currently known about this creature!
An infernal subterranean pest, the bite of a Wererat has a toxin that weakens its victim.
The large and mischievous Frost Snake uses dense balls of ice as a projectile weapon, expertly spitting at opponents from range. It is also fairly resistant to magical attacks.
Gorlok's diverse magical abilities are the result of a keen mind and assiduous studies.
A Wraith is the undead incarnation of a soul that was simply too angry to remain properly dead. It is very hard to injure and can deal considerable damage at range.
The Merfolk once had a tenuous alliance with the Helenikan Empire, but they now regard all sea-going vessels as a threat to their oceanic sovereignty.
